name: Etoricoxib
summary: One of the most COX-2-selective agents available, with once-daily dosing from a long half-life — and correspondingly closer clinical attention to blood pressure and CV risk.
good: Short courses in patients with clear GI risk and confirmed low cardiovascular risk, where once-daily dosing aids adherence.
bad: Hypertension or established cardiovascular disease — blood pressure should be monitored even in appropriate candidates.
clinicalPearls: Higher COX-2 selectivity is not simply "better" — it trades GI safety for a more pronounced cardiovascular/blood-pressure signal, illustrating the mechanism’s tradeoff directly.
mechanism: Highly selective COX-2 inhibition — among the highest COX-2:COX-1 selectivity ratios in clinical use.
originalFields: Highly selective COX-2 inhibition — among the highest COX-2:COX-1 selectivity ratios in clinical use.
Greater selectivity than celecoxib, which produces very low COX-1-mediated GI toxicity but a clearer dose-dependent blood pressure/CV signal.
Low relative to nonselective NSAIDs, consistent with high COX-2 selectivity.
Dose-dependent increases in blood pressure and cardiovascular events are more clinically prominent than with celecoxib, especially at higher doses.
Same COX-2-mediated mechanism as other agents in the class.
